test_purpose: Distribution Center receiving specialist with deep physical-receiving and inbound-transport evidence capability. Test whether Workflow Governor values physical operational expertise, uses Luis's receiving records as factual inputs to other functions, and preserves hard boundaries around Logistics routing, Q&R technical release, Procurement commercial interpretation, AP payment consequences, and Finance appeals.

error_patterns.description: When multiple systems disagree, Luis may initially privilege physical gate and receiving evidence. For Northstar-Managed Pickup, that first view can be incomplete until SRR and Ready By evidence are incorporated into responsibility analysis.
Luis may describe a receiving or dock exception as operationally resolved even though a separate commercial, payment, compliance, or financial record remains open.

should_capture: highly reliable DC receiving specialist for appointment, gate, receipt, physical condition, count, RER, seal, temperature, and receiving-disposition evidence
strong at reconstructing shipment timelines from DockSchedule, Gate Arrival, BOL, SRR, seal, photos, readings, and receiving records
strong working knowledge of inbound transportation evidence and managed-pickup readiness without possessing Logistics Manager routing authority
can make substantive same-day capacity and temporary dock/staging/unloading decisions within DC scope
separates operational containment from Q&R technical release and operational closure from later commercial or financial closure
best used as the factual operational source for Procurement, Q&R, AP, Finance, and Vendor Compliance rather than asking those functions to recreate DC evidence
should_not_claim: owns recurring Logistics lane or routing decisions because he works closely with Logistics
can release temperature, contamination, regulatory, integrity, or other Q&R technical holds
is a Procurement specialist because his evidence feeds OTIF or commercial performance decisions
can determine AP payment consequences, vendor status, chargeback dollars, or formal appeal outcomes
physical arrival or unloading proves commercial authorization, government release, or technical safety release
a dock problem being operationally closed means every linked Northstar case is closed

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: A vendor-prepaid carrier gates at 10:22 for a 10:00 appointment and Northstar assigns a door at 11:05. Luis identifies the delivery as inside the receiving arrival window.
correct_interpretation: Strong positive evidence for receiving_operations, document_comparison, evidence_evaluation, and policy_interpretation.
Door-assignment delay after compliant gate arrival should not be converted into vendor lateness.
Repeated verified work should reduce scaffolding for DockSchedule and gate-timeline decisions.
incorrect_interpretation: Door assignment rather than Gate Arrival should control the receiving arrival determination.
This success proves Luis owns the downstream Procurement OTIF or chargeback decision.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: A refrigerated load has one or more product readings above the governing specification. Luis places a Temperature Hold, expands receiving evidence, and sends the technical release decision to Q&R.
correct_interpretation: Strong positive evidence for receiving_operations, evidence_evaluation, exception_handling, and authority awareness.
Do not penalize Luis for refusing to average away an out-of-specification reading.
Routing final technical release to Q&R is correct rather than incomplete work.
incorrect_interpretation: Most acceptable readings permit Luis to release the load himself.
Returning release judgment to Q&R means Luis lacks receiving expertise.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: In a Northstar-Managed Pickup dispute, Luis initially points to the physical gate timeline, then checks the SRR and credible Ready By evidence before assigning transportation responsibility.
correct_interpretation: The initial physical-evidence emphasis is consistent with his designed work habit.
Because he incorporates SRR/Ready By evidence before concluding, this is ultimately correct cross-document reasoning.
Do not downgrade transportation_operations merely because physical evidence was his first check.
incorrect_interpretation: Gate evidence alone always determines managed-pickup responsibility.
The initial evidence preference proves a persistent false policy belief.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: Luis concludes a dock problem is resolved operationally and says so, while clearly noting that the commercial or financial follow-up remains open.
correct_interpretation: Positive evidence for boundary awareness and reporting discipline.
Operational closure and company-wide case closure are distinct.
This should support continued use of Luis for receiving resolution without implying financial authority.
incorrect_interpretation: Operational resolution automatically closes the PO, invoice, chargeback, or compliance record.
Luis must personally resolve every downstream record before the receiving task can be considered successful.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: Luis attempts to authorize a recurring lane/routing exception or release a Q&R-controlled temperature hold rather than routing the decision to Logistics or Q&R.
correct_interpretation: Treat this as an authority-boundary failure relevant to routing and verification.
Keep unrelated receiving_operations evidence local unless his physical receiving execution was also wrong.
Future similar assignments should reinforce the named owner boundary rather than remove Luis from receiving work.
incorrect_interpretation: One authority overreach proves low physical-receiving capability.
His manager title makes the recurring routing or Q&R release action valid.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: DockSchedule, Gate Arrival, receipt-date, physical count, condition, seal, RER, or receiving-disposition assessment
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: These are core explicit receiving skills and within Luis's operational authority.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: temperature or freshness receiving execution using the governing specification
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: He is explicitly skilled in receiving execution, sampling, hold initiation, and evidence capture.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: SRR, BOL, managed-pickup readiness, shipment-event, or carrier-evidence interpretation
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Transportation-document and shipment-event interpretation are explicit major skills.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: receiving or shipment evidence is incomplete or contradictory enough that the physical fact cannot be established
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Luis should request the missing operational evidence instead of inventing the timeline or condition.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: mixed receiving case plus unresolved Q&R, Procurement, AP, Finance, Vendor Compliance, or recurring Logistics decision
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Luis should complete the physical/transport-evidence portion and return the remaining decision to its owner.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: independent Procurement negotiation, vendor-status governance, invoice reconciliation, financial analysis, Q&R regulatory assessment, food-safety release, or import-compliance adjudication
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Those specialist major skills are deliberately not encoded.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: recurring lane/routing approval, Q&R technical release, Procurement commercial approval, AP payment decision, or final Finance appeal decision
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Luis's strong operational knowledge does not transfer another function's formal authority.

initially_reasonable_uncertainty: exact reliability of spreadsheet_analysis on large receiving or carrier-event datasets
how often Luis initially overweights physical gate evidence before incorporating managed-pickup readiness
whether operational-closure language consistently distinguishes downstream commercial or financial work
exact reliability of file_search beyond structured review of explicitly provided receiving and transportation records
after_relevant_evidence_should_infer: receiving_operations is highly reliable after repeated verified appointment, physical-inspection, RER, and disposition work
cross_document_reasoning and evidence_evaluation are highly reliable for shipment and receiving facts
transportation_operations is reliable for evidence interpretation and carrier/DC coordination but does not imply recurring-routing authority
temperature and freshness receiving execution is reliable when the governing specification is supplied or present in the startup policies
successful DC work should sharply reduce redundant instruction while preserving Q&R, Logistics, Procurement, AP, and Finance decision boundaries
should_remain_uncertain_without_evidence: quality_compliance as independent Q&R technical judgment
financial analysis and formal appeal adjudication

good_assignments: DockSchedule appointment and gate/receipt evidence interpretation
BOL, SRR, seal, and shipment-event interpretation
inbound incident triage and carrier/DC coordination
assign_with_scaffolding: managed-pickup responsibility cases where Procurement performance consequences are separated from Luis's SRR/Ready By evidence assessment
technical-hold cases where Luis owns containment and receiving evidence while Q&R owns release
commercial, AP, or financial cases where Luis is asked to supply authoritative DC facts rather than make the downstream decision
import-related arrivals where the relevant import release record or Import Compliance determination is supplied and Luis owns physical receiving only
normally_reassign: Procurement negotiation or commercial PO interpretation beyond the operational fact boundary
independent Q&R regulatory or food-safety release assessment
formal chargeback calculation or appeal adjudication
recurring route or lane planning that requires Logistics Manager authority
never_assign_as_authorizer: recurring appointment, lane, routing, or carrier-assignment exception reserved to Logistics
food/product-safety, contamination, temperature, integrity, regulatory, or technical-quality release reserved to Q&R
final Finance chargeback or appeal decision
verification_guidance: Use Luis's DC evidence as the authoritative physical factual input rather than asking downstream teams to reconstruct what occurred.
For Northstar-Managed Pickup responsibility, ensure SRR and Ready By evidence is considered alongside gate/receiving evidence before concluding responsibility.
Reduce redundant receiving-process review after repeated verified success, but keep authority checks at the Q&R-release and recurring-Logistics-routing boundaries.
Keep evidence updates local: an authority-boundary or operational-closure wording mistake should not erase strong receiving capability.
Treat physical arrival, unloading, or operational acceptance as evidence of DC events, not as proof of commercial authorization, government release, payment eligibility, or technical safety release.

scoring_notes: The central test is whether Workflow Governor values physical-operational expertise without turning it into universal operational authority.
Luis's startup files provide detailed receiving and transportation workflow knowledge, but detailed commercial, AP, Q&R technical, import, and financial rules remain outside his encoded knowledge.
Correctly returning Q&R release, recurring Logistics routing, Procurement commercial, AP payment, or Finance appeal decisions is successful specialization behavior.
Initial preference for physical evidence should only be penalized if Luis fails to incorporate relevant managed-pickup readiness evidence before the final responsibility conclusion.
Operational closure and downstream commercial/financial closure are separate; the evaluator should reward explicit distinction between them.
